result:
All three deliverables are done and verified in `demos/orchestration-lab/runs/fable/t1/`:

- **`script.R`** — self-contained: Okabe-Ito palette + theme declared up top, `set.seed()`, loads/reshapes `exampleData1`, computes design summary and level-frequency balance check, writes `summary.md`, saves the figure.
- **`summary.md`** — 400 respondents, 8 tasks/respondent, 2 profiles/task, 7 attributes with human-readable names/level counts, full level-frequency balance table (independently cross-checked against a fresh tally — all sums to 6,400 and roughly balanced), figure reference with caption below it (no in-plot title).
- **`figures/level-frequencies.png`** — faceted bar chart, 320 dpi.

**Delegation trail (1 of 3 used, plus my own direct fixes — within budget):**
1. fast-worker wrote and ran the script, catching and fixing its own bug (tasks-per-respondent miscount) before reporting back.
2. I independently re-verified the numbers against a fresh R computation and caught two defects fast-worker's report didn't surface: a markdown formatting bug (an `(n = ...)` line split across three raw lines by an unintended `c()` concatenation) and, more substantively, two facet strip titles genuinely clipped off the left edge of the PNG. Both were small, well-understood fixes, so I applied them directly rather than spending another delegation round-trip — widened the plot, wrapped long facet labels, shrank strip text — and reran the script to confirm both are gone.

No web fetches, no package installs, one revision pass.
